clue.text: They are the haunt of the urban snipe

definitions.text: They are the haunt of the urban snipe

parts.words: They are the haunt of the urban snipe
parts.note: the snipe here is no wading bird but the street urchin of the word ..., so his haunt is the channels at the road's edge

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes where a marsh bird might be found in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A guttersnipe is a street urchin, so the city 'snipe' lives in the drainage channels at the kerb rather than in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Street children of the guttersnipe kind are pictured living by the roadside drainage channels.

clue.text: Bird one found in bird book —-give it up

indicators.note: one is placed inside the second bird

parts.note: a gull is a sea bird
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for book is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a bird in a bird book, then abandons it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I inside GULL; 'give it up' turns TOME into EMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Britannia's aeroplane ?

parts.note: Britannia holds a three-pronged spear, which shares its name with a British airliner

explanation.surface: Asking which plane belongs to Britannia.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure of Britannia on old pennies carries a three-pronged spear; the Hawker Siddeley Trident was a British jet airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia's three-pronged spear gave its name to a 1960s British jet airliner.

clue.text: Press to follow tip found in book?

indicators.note: the press comes after the tip

parts.note: a tip is an end
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone asks about pressing a tip found inside a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as a verb but means the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Endpapers are the blank leaves pasted inside the covers of a hardback.

clue.text: Clan includes a number of Frenchmen

definitions.meaning: a branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a family branch or clan and the French for seven.

clue.text: Funny business, claim being altered

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the word claim is changed into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A comedy business is changing what it claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being altered' rearranges CLAIM into MICAL, placed after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that makes people laugh: amusing.

clue.text: Growth of brain cells possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may form another word when reordered

explanation.surface: Brain cells might be growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BRAIN CELLS. 'Growth' looks medical but means a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranesbill is a geranium, a wild plant, which is a growth of the garden.

clue.text: Beaten in game by bad team — dreadful start

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so these letters are put wrongly in order
the start of dreadful is its first letter

explanation.surface: A weak team was beaten after a dreadful opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges TEAM into MATE; 'start' takes D from 'dreadful'. The game is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a king put in checkmate means its player has lost.

clue.text: Dismiss bank employee

definitions.meaning: to discharge an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
a teller who handles money at a bank

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for discharging an officer in disgrace and a bank teller.

clue.text: Deposit by Sir Oliver

definitions.meaning: to place or ... something, as money in a bank
Sir Oliver ..., the British physicist and radio pioneer

explanation.definitionFit: To put something in safe keeping is to deposit it, and Sir Oliver was a pioneering physicist with that surname.

clue.text: Poem is one one found in youth

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the second one is placed inside the word for youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth
again the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone claims a single poem was discovered in their teenage years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts the second I inside LAD, giving LIAD after the first I; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is a famous long verse narrative.

clue.text: Trained fish to return with tides, possibly

indicators.note: returning means the fish's name is read backwards

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: possibly signals that tides may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A fish is coached to swim back in on the tides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns CARP into PRAC; 'possibly' rearranges TIDES into TISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled through repeated exercise is experienced, well drilled.

clue.text: General direction of drift

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a way is a direction, as in 'which way?'

explanation.surface: A commander's broad orientation, in the sense of the general trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective with 'direction'; it is Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, the sideways movement of a ship blown off course is its drift to leeward.

clue.text: German poet carries lad off — it's in the paper

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the other letters within it

parts.note: Heinrich Heine was a German poet

indicators.note: off signals the word lad gone awry, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A German poet carries a boy away, and the story makes the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LAD into ADL, and 'carries' puts it inside HEINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the large-type title of a newspaper story, printed in the paper.

clue.text: Love to beat up ten members, being spiteful

annotationWithheld.why: 'Love to beat up ten members, being spiteful': LAM ('to beat') reversed gives MAL and LOVE TEN rearranged gives EVOLENT, but 'members' gives nothing and no word signals the anagram
annotationWithheld.clue: Love to beat up ten members, being spiteful

clue.text: Topping episcopal joint ?

definitions.meaning: the tall headgear worn by a bishop sits on top of him
a carpenter's corner joint with two pieces cut at 45 degrees

explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed hat crowns him, and carpenters use the same name for an angled corner joint.

clue.text: Something highly scented in eccentric emir's garb

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: the word emir's, with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler's peculiar robes give off a strong perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the nine letters of EMIRS GARB; here the S of 'emir's' counts.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy substance from sperm whales is prized in perfumery for its fragrance.

clue.text: Upset over message-can be annulled

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word over is turned upside down

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a message that could be cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns OVER into REVO, before CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revocable may be withdrawn or cancelled.

clue.text: Call for help when about to mount, as it were ?

indicators.note: about means the distress signal goes round the word to

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
taken as written
a peak is a mountain top

explanation.surface: A climber calls for help just before scaling the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TO inside SOS, giving SOTOS, then PEAK follows; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases soften a figure of speech, meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Main flowers appear by spring in Derbyshire

parts.note: the main is the sea, and the things that flow in it are its tides
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Garden flowers come out in a Derbyshire spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' reads as blooms but means things that flow; 'the main' is an old word for the sea. Tideswell is a village in Derbyshire, an English county in the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: The village of that name lies in the Peak District of Derbyshire, so the place is found in that county.

clue.text: Giant organization gets praised

indicators.note: organization means arranging, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A huge company receives praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' rearranges PRAISED. Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair is a character in John Bunyan's allegory, the ogre who imprisons the pilgrims.

clue.text: Bound to have room underground

definitions.meaning: to bound is to leap, as a gymnast leaps over a horse
a cellar or burial chamber below ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a jump using the hands and an arched cellar or crypt.

clue.text: Free, but not licentious, perhaps

parts.note: un- is a prefix meaning not
loose means licentious or immoral

explanation.surface: Being free does not mean being immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says freedom is not licence, but 'not licentious' builds UN + LOOSE; 'perhaps' marks this playful construction.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to untie or release, setting free.

clue.text: Place one's back in a draught

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the draught

parts.note: a potion is a draught of medicine

indicators.note: the letters for one's are turned round

parts.note: one's gives I (one) and S

explanation.surface: Someone sets their back in a cold current of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI, and 'in' puts it inside POTION. 'draught' suggests cold air but means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to put it in a set spot or location.

clue.text: The girl for a quiet nobleman — a native product, perhaps

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A girl is matched with a soft-spoken nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The girl' is Pearl, a girl's name. A 'native' is an oyster raised in British waters, such as at Whitstable, and oysters produce gems.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed's gem forms inside shellfish; 'natives' are British oysters, so the gem is their product.

clue.text: The right name ?

definitions.meaning: a legal right to own property
a designation such as the name of a book

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a legal right of ownership and the name of a book or a rank.

clue.text: Noted practice climbs?

definitions.meaning: musicians practise runs of notes up and down
to climb up a wall is to go up it

explanation.definitionFit: Musical exercises run through the notes of a key, and the same verb means ascending a cliff.

clue.text: Highlight in animals' turn

indicators.note: turn means the word for animals is read backwards

parts.note: rats are animals

explanation.surface: A highlight in an animal act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' suggests a performance but reverses RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The main attraction of a show is its star, its highlight.

clue.text: Room apt to contain painters, perhaps

indicators.note: the word apt holds the painters within it

parts.note: taken as written
painters are an example of art men

explanation.surface: A room suitable for a crew of decorators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts ARTMEN between the P and T of APT; 'perhaps' marks painters as just one kind of art men.
explanation.definitionFit: A single room or suite in a building, also called a flat, counts as a room.

clue.text: HMS Penniless of World War!

parts.note: a Royal Navy destroyer of the First World War whose name also means having no money

explanation.surface: A warship named for having no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Broke was a British destroyer famous at the Battle of Dover Strait in 1917; 'broke' is slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for having no money doubled as the name of a British destroyer in the First World War.

clue.text: Hitler's U-boat base in the East or West of France ?

definitions.text: Hitler's U-boat base in the East or West of France ?

parts.words: Hitler's U-boat base in the East or West of France ?
parts.note: the French port's name reads as French for 'the East', yet it lies on the Atlantic coast in Brittany

explanation.surface: A geography question about where the German submarine base was.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorient, a Breton port, housed a major German U-boat base; split as L'Orient it means 'the East' in French, though the town is in the far west.
explanation.definitionFit: The Breton port in western France housed the German submarine pens in the Second World War.

clue.text: Pole's grain measure

parts.note: rye is a cereal grain
a peck is an old dry measure of two gallons

explanation.surface: A Pole's grain measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a pole used to moor a punt on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A rye-peck is an iron-shod pole driven into a riverbed to moor a punt.
